questions.question: As an NBFC-MFI, which RBI directions must we follow for the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities when computing capital?
questions.answer: An NBFC-MFI must adhere to the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 for the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities in its capital computation.
questions.evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall also adhere to provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 on treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for computation of capital.

questions.question: For an NBFC-MFI, which deferred tax items are covered by the capital-computation requirement?
questions.answer: Both deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are covered, and the NBFC-MFI must follow the 2025 NBFC Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions for their treatment.
questions.evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall also adhere to provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 on treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for computation of capital.

unanswerable.question: What percentage of deferred tax assets may an NBFC-MFI include when computing its capital?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states no percentage or recognition limit; it only requires adherence to the deferred-tax treatment in the 2025 NBFC Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions.

questions.question: As an NBFC-MFI acting as a channelizing agent for a Central or State Government loan scheme, how should those scheme loans be treated when checking the minimum threshold of microfinance loans?
questions.answer: They must be treated as a separate business segment, and the scheme loans must be excluded from both the microfinance-loan numerator and the total-assets denominator used to assess compliance with the minimum threshold.
questions.evidence: Loans disbursed or managed by the NBFC-MFI in its capacity as channelizing agent for Central / State Government Agencies shall be considered as a separate business segment. These loans shall not be included either in the numerator (microfinance loans) or the denominator (total assets) for the purpose of determining compliance with the minimum threshold of microfinance loans.

questions.question: For an NBFC-MFI distributing loans under a special Central or State Government scheme, to whom must the loans be reported, and what is the purpose of that reporting?
questions.answer: All such loans must be reported to Credit Information Companies. The reporting is intended to prevent multiple borrowings and present a complete picture of a borrower's indebtedness.
questions.evidence: all such loans shall be reported to Credit Information Companies to prevent multiple borrowings and present complete picture of indebtedness of a borrower.

unanswerable.question: What minimum percentage of an NBFC-MFI's total assets must consist of microfinance loans to meet the required threshold?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers to a minimum threshold for microfinance loans but does not state the percentage, amount, or calculation needed to meet it.

questions.question: For an NBFC-MFI, how must standard assets on microfinance loans be provisioned when the loans fall within a particular layer of the scale-based regulatory framework?
questions.answer: The NBFC-MFI must follow the instructions in the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 for the layer in which the loans fall.
questions.evidence: Standard assets provisioning of microfinance loans of an NBFC-MFI lying in a particular layer of the scale based regulatory framework shall be in accordance with instructions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 for the respective layer.

questions.question: Which RBI Directions apply to standard-asset provisioning by an NBFC-MFI for microfinance loans classified within a layer of the scale-based regulatory framework?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 apply, using the instructions applicable to the respective layer.
questions.evidence: Standard assets provisioning of microfinance loans of an NBFC-MFI lying in a particular layer of the scale based regulatory framework shall be in accordance with instructions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 for the respective layer.

unanswerable.question: What provisioning percentage must an NBFC-MFI apply to standard microfinance assets in each layer of the scale-based regulatory framework?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers to layer-specific instructions in the 2025 Directions but does not state any provisioning percentage or rate.

questions.question: For an NBFC organized as a not-for-profit company that is not eligible for the referenced exemptions, what registration and compliance obligations apply?
questions.answer: It must register as an NBFC-MFI, adhere to the regulations applicable to NBFC-MFIs, and submit its registration application to the Reserve Bank.
questions.evidence: ‘Not for profit’ companies that are not eligible for the exemptions mentioned above are required to register as NBFC-MFIs and adhere to the regulations applicable to NBFC-MFIs. Such companies shall submit the application for registration as an NBFC-MFI to the Reserve Bank.

questions.question: For an NBFC that currently does not comply with NBFC-MFI regulations, what must accompany its registration application to the Reserve Bank?
questions.answer: It must submit a board-approved plan containing a roadmap for meeting the prescribed NBFC-MFI regulations.
questions.evidence: Those companies that currently do not comply with the regulations prescribed for NBFC-MFIs, shall submit a board-approved plan, with a roadmap to meet the prescribed regulations, along with their application for registration.

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must a not-for-profit NBFC that currently does not comply with NBFC-MFI regulations submit its board-approved compliance plan and registration application?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires submission of the plan and application but does not specify any deadline or time period for doing so.

questions.question: Does the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025 apply to my NBFC-MFI if it is registered with the RBI under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934?
questions.answer: Yes. The Directions apply to every NBFC-MFI registered with the Reserve Bank under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
questions.evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (hereinafter collectively referred to as ‘NBFC-MFIs’ and individually as an ‘NBFC-MFI’) registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

questions.question: Under which statute must an NBFC-MFI be registered with the RBI for the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025 to apply?
questions.answer: It must be registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).
questions.evidence: registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC-MFI have after registration with the RBI to comply with the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the scope of applicability but does not specify any compliance deadline or period for implementation.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what conditions do I need to satisfy to be classified as an NBFC-MFI under the RBI's microfinance institution directions?
questions.answer: You must be a non-deposit taking NBFC and have at least 60 percent of your total assets, after netting off intangible assets, deployed towards microfinance loans on an ongoing basis.
questions.evidence: “NBFC-MFI” means a non-deposit taking NBFC which has a minimum of 60 percent of its total assets (netted off by intangible assets) deployed towards “microfinance loans” on an ongoing basis.

questions.question: As an NBFC-MFI, how do the RBI's microfinance institution directions define Tier 1 capital and Tier 2 capital?
questions.answer: Both are set by reference to the prudential norms: Tier 1 capital and Tier 2 capital have the same elements as prescribed in the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: “Tier 1 capital” shall have the same elements as prescribed in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025. (7) “Tier 2 capital” shall have the same elements as prescribed in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.

unanswerable.question: What minimum Tier 1 capital ratio must an NBFC-MFI maintain as a percentage of its risk-weighted assets?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital have the same elements as prescribed in the prudential norms directions; it does not state any minimum capital adequacy percentage or ratio for NBFC-MFIs.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC, is the MD & CEO allowed to attend the Board meeting at which their own accountability is being examined?
questions.answer: No. A very senior executive whose accountability is being considered must stay out of the Board, Audit Committee, or SCBMF meeting at which that accountability is discussed.
questions.evidence: Such executives shall not participate in the meeting of the Board / ACB / SCBMF in which its accountability is to be considered.

questions.question: For an NBFC in the public sector, is there any additional step required when a case concerns a very senior executive such as an Executive Director?
questions.answer: Yes. In addition to the examination by the Audit Committee and placement before the Board, such cases in a public sector NBFC must also be referred to the ABBFF.
questions.evidence: However, in case of the Applicable NBFC in the public sector, such cases shall also be referred to the ABBFF.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC's Audit Committee complete the examination of a very senior executive's accountability and place the matter before the Board?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the ACB to initiate the examination and place it before the Board, but it states no time limit, deadline, or maximum number of days for doing so.

questions.question: Can an NBFC include terms in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable when their wilful negligence or malpractice contributes to fraud?
questions.answer: Yes. An Applicable NBFC may include necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable where their wilful negligence or malpractice is found to be a causative factor for fraud.
questions.evidence: Therefore, the Applicable NBFC may incorporate necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable in situations where wilful negligence / malpractice by them is found to be a causative factor for fraud.

questions.question: At which stages of the lending process does an NBFC rely on third-party service providers?
questions.answer: An Applicable NBFC relies on third-party service providers during pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC places reliance on various third-party service providers as part of pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring.

unanswerable.question: What percentage of an NBFC's pre-sanction appraisal work may be outsourced to third-party service providers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any percentage, numerical cap, or outsourcing limit for pre-sanction appraisal.

questions.question: What should an NBFC's policy on hiring external auditors cover?
questions.answer: It should cover due diligence, the auditors' competency and track record, and other relevant aspects.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall frame a policy on engagement of external auditors covering aspects such as due diligence, competency and track record of the auditors, among others.

questions.question: What timing clauses should an NBFC include in its contract with external auditors?
questions.answer: The contract should set out a timeline for completing the audit and require submission of the audit report to the NBFC within a specified time limit approved by the Board.
questions.evidence: the contractual agreement with the auditors shall, inter alia, contain suitable clauses on timeline for completion of the audit and submission of audit report to the Applicable NBFC within a specified time limit, as approved by the Board.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days an NBFC has to submit the external audit report after the audit is completed?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a specified time limit approved by the Board but does not state any particular number of days or concrete deadline.

questions.question: As an NBFC, if applying the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Companies Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026 proves difficult, can the RBI issue clarifications, and would its interpretation bind us?
questions.answer: Yes. The RBI may, if it considers it necessary, issue clarifications on any matter covered by the Directions, and its interpretation of any provision is final and binding.
questions.evidence: RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein and the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by RBI shall be final and binding.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Companies Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026, on what grounds and regarding which matters may the RBI issue clarifications?
questions.answer: The RBI may issue clarifications either to give effect to the provisions of the Directions or to remove difficulties in their application or interpretation, and the clarifications may relate to any matter covered by the Directions.
questions.evidence: For giving effect to the provisions of these Directions or to remove any difficulties in the application or interpretation of the provisions of these Directions, RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein

unanswerable.question: How long does an NBFC have to comply with a clarification issued by the RBI under the Non-Banking Financial Companies Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 62 states no compliance deadline, response period, or effective date for NBFCs in relation to RBI clarifications; it only addresses the RBI's power to issue clarifications and the final and binding nature of its interpretation.

questions.question: What aspects of fraud risk management must an NBFC's internal audit function review?
questions.answer: An NBFC's internal audit must cover the controls and processes for preventing, detecting, classifying, monitoring, reporting, closing and withdrawing fraud cases, as well as weaknesses in critical processes of the fraud risk management framework.
questions.evidence: Internal Audit in the Applicable NBFC shall cover controls and processes involved in prevention, detection, classification, monitoring, reporting, closure and withdrawal of fraud cases, as well as weaknesses observed in the critical processes in the fraud risk management framework of the Applicable NBFC

questions.question: Which specific reporting and accountability weaknesses should an NBFC's internal audit examine?
questions.answer: The internal audit should examine delays in reporting fraud, failures to report fraud, the conduct of staff accountability examinations, and prudential provisioning.
questions.evidence: including delay in reporting, non-reporting, conduct of staff accountability examination and prudential provisioning.

unanswerable.question: How many fraud cases must an NBFC's internal audit review each financial year?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph sets out what internal audit must cover but states no annual review count, sampling rate, or other numerical threshold for the number of fraud cases to be examined.

questions.question: Can an NBFC withdraw its FMR or remove a fraud perpetrator's name from that report, and when is this permitted?
questions.answer: Yes. An NBFC may withdraw the FMR or remove the perpetrator's name from it under exceptional circumstances.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC may, under exceptional circumstances, withdraw FMR / remove name(s) of perpetrator(s) from FMR.

questions.question: What justification and approval are required when an NBFC removes a fraud perpetrator's name from its FMR?
questions.answer: The removal must be made with due justification and approved by an official at least in the rank of a director.
questions.evidence: Such withdrawal / removal shall, however, be made with due justification and with the approval of an official at least in the rank of a director.

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have to complete the withdrawal of its FMR or the removal of a perpetrator's name after an exceptional circumstance arises?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits withdrawal or removal under exceptional circumstances and requires due justification and director-level approval, but it specifies no deadline.

questions.question: As an NBFC, by when must we report a robbery or attempted theft to the RBI?
questions.answer: An NBFC must report the incident immediately and, in any event, no later than seven days after it occurs.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall report instances of theft, burglary, dacoity and robbery (including attempted cases), to Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG), Department of Supervision, Central Office, Reserve Bank of India, immediately (not later than seven days) from their occurrence

questions.question: As an NBFC, where and how should we submit the report for a theft or dacoity?
questions.answer: Submit it in the prescribed RBR format by email to the Fraud Monitoring Group in the RBI’s Department of Supervision, Central Office, at fmgconbfc@rbi.org.in.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall report instances of theft, burglary, dacoity and robbery (including attempted cases), to Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG), Department of Supervision, Central Office, Reserve Bank of India, immediately (not later than seven days) from their occurrence, in the prescribed ‘Return on Bank Robberies, Dacoities, Thefts and Burglaries (RBR)’ format through e-mail ( fmgconbfc@rbi.org.in).

unanswerable.question: What minimum monetary loss must an NBFC have suffered before it must report a theft or robbery to the RBI?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires reporting all instances, including attempted cases, but does not state any monetary threshold.

questions.question: Before an NBFC transfers a loan account or credit facility to another lender or an Asset Reconstruction Company, what fraud-related review must it complete?
questions.answer: The NBFC must complete an investigation from the fraud angle before the transfer.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall complete the investigation from fraud angle before transferring the loan account / credit facility to other lenders / Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs).

questions.question: After an NBFC sells an account to an Asset Reconstruction Company, what must it do to keep the RBI informed about later developments in that account?
questions.answer: It must continue reporting subsequent developments to the RBI and periodically obtain the required information from the ARC.
questions.evidence: In cases where accounts are sold to ARCs, the Applicable NBFC shall continue to report subsequent developments in such accounts to RBI, by obtaining requisite information periodically from the concerned ARCs.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC obtain information from an ARC to support its subsequent reporting of developments to the RBI?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires periodic information and reporting but does not specify a frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: When an NBFC suspects wrongdoing or fraudulent activity in a loan account, what investigation is required?
questions.answer: The NBFC must use either an external audit or an internal audit, in accordance with its Board-approved Policy, to investigate the account further.
questions.evidence: In case where there is a suspicion / indication of wrongdoing or fraudulent activity, the Applicable NBFC shall use an external audit or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy for further investigation in such accounts.

questions.question: What approval is required for the NBFC's policy governing audits of accounts with suspected fraud?
questions.answer: The policy must be approved by the NBFC's Board.
questions.evidence: the Applicable NBFC shall use an external audit or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy for further investigation in such accounts.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC complete the audit of an account after suspecting fraudulent activity?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires an audit for further investigation but does not specify any deadline for completing it.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what must be completed before we can close a reported fraud case through the Closure Module?
questions.answer: An NBFC must ensure that fraud cases pending with law enforcement agencies or a court have been disposed of and that the examination of staff accountability has been completed.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall close fraud cases using ‘Closure Module’ where the actions as stated below are complete: (1) The fraud cases pending with LEAs / Court are disposed of; and (2) The examination of staff accountability has been completed.

questions.question: Can an NBFC close a fraud case through the Closure Module if its staff-accountability examination is still incomplete?
questions.answer: No. The staff-accountability examination must be completed, along with disposal of any fraud case pending with law enforcement agencies or a court.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall close fraud cases using ‘Closure Module’ where the actions as stated below are complete: (1) The fraud cases pending with LEAs / Court are disposed of; and (2) The examination of staff accountability has been completed.

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have to complete the staff-accountability examination after a court disposes of a fraud case?
unanswerable.why: No deadline or number of days is specified for completing the staff-accountability examination; the only stated requirement is that it be completed before closure.

questions.question: If an NBFC identifies a borrowal account as fraudulent, which other accounts must it examine for possible fraud?
questions.answer: It must examine the borrowal accounts of other group companies that share at least one promoter or whole-time director with the company whose account was identified as fraudulent.
questions.evidence: In case an account is identified as a fraud by any Applicable NBFC, the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

questions.question: Can an NBFC's duty to examine related borrowal accounts be triggered by fraud identified by a different applicable NBFC?
questions.answer: Yes. Identification of an account as fraud by any applicable NBFC triggers examination of the borrowal accounts of other group companies sharing one or more promoters or whole-time directors.
questions.evidence: the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC complete the fraud-angle examination of related group companies' borrowal accounts?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the examination but does not specify a deadline or time period for completing it.

questions.question: For an Upper Layer or Middle Layer NBFC, what must we build into our early warning system (EWS) to monitor other financial or non-credit-related transactions?
questions.answer: The NBFC must develop or strengthen its EWS by identifying suitable indicators and parameterising them to monitor these transactions. It must also strive to continuously upgrade the system, improve its integrity and robustness, and prevent fraudulent activities.
questions.evidence: NBFCs - UL and ML shall develop / strengthen their EWS system by identifying suitable indicators and parameterising them in their EWS system for monitoring other financial / non-credit related transactions. NBFCs - UL and ML shall strive to continuously upgrade the EWS system for enhancing its integrity and robustness, monitor other financial / non-credit related transactions efficiently and prevent fraudulent activities.

questions.question: What must an Upper Layer or Middle Layer NBFC do to confirm that its EWS for other financial and non-credit-related transactions is effective?
questions.answer: It must test the effectiveness of its EWS system periodically.
questions.evidence: Further, the effectiveness of EWS system shall be tested periodically.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permitted interval between effectiveness tests of an Upper Layer or Middle Layer NBFC's EWS system for other financial and non-credit-related transactions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires periodic testing but does not specify a testing interval, maximum period, or deadline.

questions.question: As an NBFC, where in our financial statements do we need to report the amount of fraud for the year?
questions.answer: You must disclose the fraud amount reported in the company for the year in the Notes to Accounts of your Financial Statements.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall disclose the amount related to fraud reported in the company for the year in its Financial Statements – Notes to Accounts.

questions.question: Does the requirement to disclose fraud amounts in the Notes to Accounts apply to every NBFC, or only to NBFCs in the Upper Layer and Middle Layer?
questions.answer: It applies only to NBFCs in the Upper Layer and Middle Layer, because Chapter III, which contains this disclosure requirement, is restricted to those two layers.
questions.evidence: Chapter III - Framework for Early Warning Signals for Detection of Frauds (NBFCs in the Upper Layer and Middle Layer only)

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum amount of fraud that an NBFC must disclose in the Notes to Accounts for the year?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires disclosure of the amount of fraud reported but does not state any minimum threshold, reporting deadline, or other numeric condition for disclosure.

questions.question: As an NBFC that lends against gold and silver collateral, what must I publish on my website about the weight of the metal in the collateral?
questions.answer: I must publish the methodology I use to determine the net weight of the gold and silver content in eligible collateral.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral

questions.question: As an NBFC offering loans against gold and silver collateral, what valuation information must I publish on my website for calculating the LTV ratio?
questions.answer: I must publish the price used to value the gold and silver content of eligible collateral when determining the LTV ratio.
questions.evidence: shall display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral and the price used to value the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral for determination of LTV ratio.

unanswerable.question: As an NBFC, how frequently must I refresh the gold and silver valuation price and net-weight methodology published on my website?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires website display of the methodology and price but does not state any refresh interval, deadline, or frequency.

questions.question: For an NBFC collecting microfinance loans, during what hours must it avoid calling borrowers, and what calling pattern is also prohibited?
questions.answer: An NBFC must not persistently call a microfinance borrower, nor call that borrower before 9:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m.
questions.evidence: Persistently calling the borrower and/ or calling the borrower before 9:00 a.m. and after 6:00 p.m.

questions.question: For an NBFC recovering microfinance loans, what conduct involving publication of borrower details, threats, or misleading information is forbidden?
questions.answer: An NBFC must not publish borrowers’ names, use or threaten violence or similar harm to the borrower or the borrower’s family, assets, or reputation, or mislead the borrower about the debt or the consequences of non-repayment.
questions.evidence: (4) Publishing the names of borrowers (5) Use or threat of use of violence or other similar means to harm the borrower or borrower’s family/ assets/ reputation (6) Misleading the borrower about the extent of the debt or the consequences of non-repayment

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of collection calls an NBFC may make to a microfinance borrower in one day?
unanswerable.why: The cited provision prohibits persistent calling and calls before 9:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m., but it does not specify a daily numerical limit on calls.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what information must we include on a loan application form so that borrowers can compare our offer with another lender's terms?
questions.answer: An NBFC's loan application form must include information affecting the borrower's interest, enabling a meaningful comparison with another lender's terms and conditions and an informed borrowing decision.
questions.evidence: Loan application forms shall include necessary information which affects the interest of the borrower, so that a meaningful comparison with the terms and conditions offered by another lender can be made, and informed decision can be taken by the borrower.

questions.question: What should an NBFC tell borrowers about the documents they need to provide when applying for a loan?
questions.answer: The NBFC's loan application form must identify the documents that borrowers are required to submit with it.
questions.evidence: The loan application form shall indicate the documents required to be submitted with the application form.

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have to acknowledge a borrower's loan application after receiving it?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires certain information and document details to appear on loan application forms, but it does not state any deadline for acknowledging a loan application.

questions.question: As an NBFC offering loans secured by gold or silver, where must the pledged collateral be kept?
questions.answer: The pledged collateral must be kept only at NBFC branches staffed by the company’s employees and equipped with safe deposit vaults suitable for gold and silver.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall store the collateral only in its branches which are manned by its employees and having safe deposit vaults fit for storing gold and silver.

questions.question: Can an NBFC branch that lacks a secure storage area continue making loans against pledged gold or silver?
questions.answer: Normally, it cannot. A branch without an appropriate secured facility for storing the pledged eligible collateral should not extend such loans.
questions.evidence: Normally, such loans shall not be extended by branches that do not have appropriate secured facility for storage of the pledged eligible collateral.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum number of employees an NBFC branch must have on duty to store gold or silver collateral?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires collateral to be held at branches manned by the NBFC’s employees, but it does not specify any minimum staffing number.

questions.question: As an NBFC, when must I release securities held against a borrower after repayment or realisation of the outstanding loan amount?
questions.answer: An NBFC must release all securities once all dues are repaid or the outstanding loan amount is realised, unless it has a legitimate right or lien for another claim against the borrower.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall release all securities on repayment of all dues or on realisation of the outstanding amount of loan subject to any legitimate right or lien for any other claim they may have against borrower.

questions.question: If an NBFC intends to exercise a right of set-off and retain a borrower’s securities, what notice must it provide?
questions.answer: It must notify the borrower and give full particulars of the remaining claims and the conditions under which the securities may be retained until the relevant claim is settled or paid.
questions.evidence: If such right of set off is to be exercised, the borrower shall be given notice about the same with full particulars about the remaining claims and the conditions under which the NBFC is entitled to retain the securities till the relevant claim is settled / paid.

unanswerable.question: How many days in advance must an NBFC notify a borrower before exercising set-off and retaining the borrower’s securities?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires notice but does not specify any minimum notice period or number of days.

questions.question: As an NBFC, how frequently must we place a report on unclaimed gold or silver collateral before the Customer Service Committee or Board for review?
questions.answer: The report must be placed before the Customer Service Committee or Board, as applicable, at half-yearly intervals.
questions.evidence: A report on unclaimed gold and /or silver collateral shall be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, as the case may be, at half-yearly intervals for a review.

questions.question: For an NBFC, which body should receive the report on unclaimed gold and silver collateral for review?
questions.answer: The report should be placed before the Customer Service Committee or the Board, as the case may be.
questions.evidence: A report on unclaimed gold and /or silver collateral shall be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, as the case may be, at half-yearly intervals for a review.

unanswerable.question: What exact due date should an NBFC meet when submitting the report on unclaimed gold and silver collateral at each half-yearly review?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies half-yearly intervals but does not state a fixed submission date or deadline.

questions.question: As an NBFC that lends to microfinance borrowers, what must we put in place before hiring recovery agents to collect overdue dues?
questions.answer: The NBFC must have a due diligence process for engaging recovery agents, and that process must cover the individuals involved in the recovery process.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall have a due diligence process in place for engagement of recovery agents, which shall, inter alia, cover individuals involved in the recovery process.

questions.question: For recovery agents working on an NBFC's microfinance loans, what background checks are required on the agents' own employees, and who sets how often those checks are repeated?
questions.answer: The recovery agents must verify the antecedents of their employees, which includes police verification. The NBFC must decide the periodicity at which re-verification of those antecedents is carried out.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall also ensure that the recovery agents engaged by them carry out verification of the antecedents of its employees, which shall include police verification. The NBFC shall also decide the periodicity at which re-verification of antecedents shall be resorted to.

unanswerable.question: How long before a recovery agent begins collecting microfinance loan dues must an NBFC obtain police verification of that agent's employees?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a due diligence process for engaging recovery agents, police verification of their employees' antecedents, and an NBFC-decided periodicity for re-verification, but it states no deadline or time period for completing the initial verification.

questions.question: For an NBFC, from what date do the RBI requirements for releasing original property documents after repayment or settlement of a personal loan apply?
questions.answer: They apply to cases where the release of the original documents falls due on or after December 1, 2023.
questions.evidence: The instructions contained under this section shall be applicable to all cases where release of original movable / immovable property documents falls due on or after December 1, 2023.

questions.question: If an NBFC provides compensation under the RBI rules for releasing property documents after a personal loan is repaid or settled, can the borrower still seek other compensation available under applicable law?
questions.answer: Yes. The compensation is without prejudice to the borrower’s right to obtain any other compensation available under applicable law.
questions.evidence: Further, the compensation provided under these directions shall be without prejudice to the rights of a borrower to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.

unanswerable.question: What amount or percentage of compensation must an NBFC pay for delaying the release of original property documents after a personal loan is repaid?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify a compensation amount, percentage, calculation method, or payment deadline; it only preserves a borrower’s right to seek other compensation under applicable law.

questions.question: When an NBFC accepts gold or silver as eligible collateral, what information must its assay certificate or e-certificate contain?
questions.answer: It must state the purity in carats, gross and net gold or silver weights, any deductions for stones, lac, alloys, strings, fastenings and similar items, any damage, breakage or defects, an image of the collateral, and the collateral’s value.
questions.evidence: state therein the purity (in terms of carats); gross weight of the eligible collateral pledged; net weight of gold or silver content therein and deductions, if any, relating to weight of stones, lac, alloy, strings, fastenings, etc.; damage, breakage or defects, if any, noticed in the collateral; image of the collateral; and the value of collateral

questions.question: What must an NBFC do with the two copies of the assay certificate or e-certificate for gold or silver collateral?
questions.answer: The NBFC must retain one copy as part of the loan documents and give the other copy to the borrower against the borrower’s acknowledgement.
questions.evidence: One copy of the certificate or e-certificate shall be kept as part of the loan documents and the other copy shall be given to the borrower under her / his acknowledgement.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days after accepting eligible gold or silver collateral must an NBFC prepare the assay certificate and deliver a copy to the borrower?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the certificate and specifies how the copies must be handled, but it does not state any deadline for preparing or delivering it.

questions.question: As an NBFC, at financial closure of a project loan, should an approval that depends on completing a project milestone be treated as a mandatory pre-requisite?
questions.answer: No. It is applicable only after the relevant milestone is achieved and is not a mandatory pre-requisite at the time of financial closure.
questions.evidence: Approvals / clearances which are contingent upon achievement of certain milestones in terms of project completion shall be deemed to be applicable only when such milestones are achieved.

questions.question: For an NBFC financing a project that includes a boiler, when can consent to operate the boiler be treated as an applicable approval condition?
questions.answer: It can be treated as applicable only after the boiler has been constructed; consent to operate cannot be applied for before construction.
questions.evidence: For example, consent to operate a boiler can only be applied for after the construction of a boiler. Hence, the same shall not be treated as an applicable mandatory pre-requisite at the time of financial closure.

unanswerable.question: How long after the relevant project milestone is achieved must an NBFC obtain the contingent approval before disbursing the loan?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph says the approval becomes applicable only when the milestone is achieved, but it specifies no deadline for obtaining the approval or waiting period before disbursement.

questions.question: Which activities should an NBFC include in its board-approved credit policy?
questions.answer: An NBFC's policy must cover digital lending (including DLG), lending against gold and silver collateral, microfinance loans, project finance, demand/call loans, and housing finance, insofar as the NBFC undertakes those activities.
questions.evidence:
An NBFC shall put in place Board approved credit policy covering, inter alia, the areas specified below, to the extent such activities are undertaken by it.
(1) Digital Lending including DLG
(2) Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral
(3) Microfinance Loans
(4) Project Finance
(5) Demand / Call Loans
(6) Housing Finance

questions.question: Must an NBFC include housing finance in its board-approved credit policy if it does not undertake any housing finance activity?
questions.answer: No. An NBFC need only cover the listed activities to the extent it actually undertakes them.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall put in place Board approved credit policy covering, inter alia, the areas specified below, to the extent such activities are undertaken by it.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC's board review and update its credit policy for digital lending and the other covered activities?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a board-approved credit policy and identifies the activities it must cover, but it does not state any review or update frequency.

questions.question: How does an NBFC classify a financed project into stages for applying the RBI's prudential guidelines, and what activities are covered in the design stage?
questions.answer: The RBI broadly divides projects into three phases: design, construction, and operational. The design phase runs from the genesis of the project through designing, planning, and obtaining all applicable clearances and approvals, up to financial closure.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of application of prudential guidelines contained in this Chapter, Projects shall be broadly divided into three phases namely: (1) Design phase – This is the first phase which starts with the genesis of the project and includes, inter-alia, designing, planning, obtaining all applicable clearances / approvals till its financial closure.

questions.question: Under the RBI's prudential guidelines for NBFCs, when does the operational phase of a project begin and when does it end?
questions.answer: It begins on the day the project actually commences commercial operation, i.e., the actual DCCO, and continues until the project finance exposure has been fully repaid.
questions.evidence: (3) Operational Phase – This is the last phase which starts with commencement of commercial operation by the project on the day of the actual DCCO and ends with full repayment of the project finance exposure.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days an NBFC may allow for the design phase of a project to continue before the project must be treated as stalled or classified as non-performing?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph sets out the three project phases and their boundaries but states no time limit, grace period, or delay-triggered classification rule for the design phase.

questions.question: As an NBFC, can I take a loan by using the gold or silver that a borrower has pledged to me as collateral?
questions.answer: No. An NBFC may not avail itself of loans by re-pledging gold or silver pledged to it by its borrowers.
questions.evidence: (1) Avail loans by re-pledging gold or silver pledged to it by its borrowers.

questions.question: Can an NBFC finance another lender against underlying receivables, even though it cannot accept gold or silver that its borrower has pledged to that lender?
questions.answer: Yes. The restriction does not preclude a lender from financing another lender against the security of underlying receivables.
questions.evidence: (2) Extend loans to other lenders, entities or individuals by accepting gold or silver collateral pledged to such lenders, entities, or individuals by their borrowers as collateral. For removal of doubt, it is clarified that the above provision does not preclude a lender from financing another lender against the security of underlying receivables.

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must an NBFC report any re-pledging of borrower-pledged gold or silver to the Reserve Bank of India?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph prohibits re-pledging but does not prescribe any reporting requirement or deadline for such activity.

questions.question: As an NBFC, where in our financial statements are we required to make the prescribed disclosures?
questions.answer: An NBFC must make the disclosures in its financial statements under ‘Notes to Accounts’, in accordance with the RBI’s NBFCs – Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall make appropriate disclosures in their financial statements, under ‘Notes to Accounts’, as specified in the Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: As an NBFC, which RBI framework governs the presentation and disclosure requirements for our financial statements?
questions.answer: The applicable framework is the Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall make appropriate disclosures in their financial statements, under ‘Notes to Accounts’, as specified in the Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures) Directions, 2025.

unanswerable.question: What specific disclosure items must an NBFC include in the Notes to Accounts for credit facilities provided to borrowers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires NBFC disclosures in the Notes to Accounts and identifies the applicable presentation and disclosure framework, but it does not enumerate the specific disclosure items.

questions.question: As an NBFC compliance officer, what is the maximum DLG cover I can maintain on a loan portfolio designated upfront?
questions.answer: The total DLG cover must not exceed 5% of the total amount disbursed from that loan portfolio at any given time.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall ensure that the total amount of DLG cover on any outstanding portfolio which is specified upfront shall not exceed five per cent of the total amount disbursed out of that loan portfolio at any given time.

questions.question: If an NBFC has invoked its DLG cover on defaulted loans and subsequently recovers money, can it use that recovery to restore the available DLG headroom?
questions.answer: No. A recovery on the defaulted loans cannot be added back to reinstate the DLG cover.
questions.evidence: However, the recovery amount of ₹1 crore cannot be added to reinstate the DLG cover.

unanswerable.question: What minimum credit rating or net worth must a DLG provider meet to be eligible for a DLG arrangement with an NBFC?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 24 specifies the DLG cap and the composition of the DLG set, but it does not state any credit-rating, net-worth, or other eligibility condition for DLG providers.

questions.question: As an NBFC, how do we decide whether a loan we originate is to be treated as commercial real estate exposure?
questions.answer: A loan qualifies as CRE if it is extended to builders, developers or others for purposes such as office buildings, retail space, industrial or warehouse space, hotels, land, acquisition, development or construction, and the prospects of repayment or recovery on default depend primarily on the cash flows generated by the asset through lease or rental payments or sale.
questions.evidence: loan to builders/ developers/ other for office building, retail space, multi-purpose commercial premises, multitenant commercial premises, industrial or warehouse space, hotels, land, acquisition, development and construction etc. where the prospects for repayment, or recovery in case of default, would depend primarily on the cash flows generated by the asset by way of lease / rental payments, sale etc.

questions.question: For an NBFC, starting from which dwelling unit does a loan taken by an individual get classified as commercial real estate exposure?
questions.answer: Loans for the third dwelling unit onwards to an individual are treated as CRE exposure.
questions.evidence: Further, loans for third dwelling unit onwards to an individual will be treated as CRE exposure.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum loan-to-value ratio an NBFC may offer when financing a commercial real estate project?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph explains what qualifies as CRE exposure and when loans to individuals for additional dwelling units are reclassified as CRE, but it states no loan-to-value ratio, valuation norm, tenor limit or any other numeric condition for CRE lending.

questions.question: May an NBFC open a customer account in a fictitious or benami name?
questions.answer: No. An NBFC is prohibited from opening any account in an anonymous or fictitious or benami name.
questions.evidence: not open any account in an anonymous or fictitious / benami name.

questions.question: For an NBFC, if a customer already has a KYC-compliant account and wants another account or service from the same NBFC, must the NBFC repeat the full CDD identification exercise?
questions.answer: No, not for identification of the customer. CDD is applied at the UCIC level, so no fresh CDD exercise is needed when the same KYC-compliant customer obtains another account, product or service from the same NBFC.
questions.evidence: apply the CDD procedure at the Unique Customer Identification Customer (UCIC) level. Thus, if an existing KYC-compliant customer of an NBFC desires to open another account or avail of any other product or service from the same NBFC, there shall be no need for a fresh CDD exercise as far as identification of the customer is concerned.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC refresh an existing customer's KYC information under its periodic updation process?
unanswerable.why: The rulebook requires an NBFC to specify the information sought during periodic KYC updation, but it does not state any refresh interval or deadline.

questions.question: What should an NBFC do if it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing and believes that customer due diligence would alert the customer?
questions.answer: It must not pursue the customer due diligence process. Instead, it must file an STR with FIU-IND.
questions.evidence: Where the NBFC forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

questions.question: What conditions must an NBFC meet before refraining from customer due diligence because of a money-laundering or terrorist-financing suspicion?
questions.answer: The NBFC must have formed a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing and reasonably believe that performing CDD would tip off the customer. It must then refrain from pursuing CDD and file an STR with FIU-IND instead.
questions.evidence: Where the NBFC forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC file the STR with FIU-IND after deciding not to pursue customer due diligence because the customer might be tipped off?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the NBFC to file an STR with FIU-IND but does not specify any deadline for doing so.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, do the interest-rate directions in paragraph 6 also apply to rupee advances granted against FCNR(B) deposits for a third party?
questions.answer: Yes. Those directions also apply to rupee advances made against FCNR(B) deposits for a third party.
questions.evidence: The directions contained in paragraph 6 above shall also be applicable to Rupee advances granted against FCNR(B) deposits to a third party or out of resources mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, do the interest-rate directions in paragraph 6 also cover rupee advances funded from resources mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme?
questions.answer: Yes. The paragraph 6 directions also apply to rupee advances made out of resources mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme.
questions.evidence: The directions contained in paragraph 6 above shall also be applicable to Rupee advances granted against FCNR(B) deposits to a third party or out of resources mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme.

unanswerable.question: For a commercial bank, what is the maximum interest rate permitted on a rupee advance granted against an FCNR(B) deposit for a third party?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the paragraph 6 directions apply, but it does not specify any interest-rate ceiling or numerical pricing limit for these advances.
